A1.notes.Q3: Course performance data seems useful but sensitive. Absalon data feels intrusive. Disability and race/ethnicity data raise significant ethical concerns.
A1.notes.Q4: High explainability is crucial for trust and appropriate support. Moderate explainability could be acceptable with some improvement.
A1.notes.Q5: Ensuring the model works equally well across groups is important, but not at the cost of missing too many students in need.
A1.notes.Q6: Personalized outreach and meetings are more effective but also more resource-intensive. Twice a year seems like a reasonable balance.
A1.notes.Q7: For generic emails, aiming for a balance is important to not overwhelm students or advisors. For personalized outreach, it's better to be selective.
A1.Q8.1: It would be helpful to understand how the model will be integrated into existing support systems and workflows.

A2.notes.Q3: Need to balance privacy concerns with identifying at-risk students.
A2.notes.Q4: Clear explanations are crucial for trust and effective support.
A2.notes.Q5: Ensuring all groups have equal access to support is essential.
A2.notes.Q6: General information with optional personalized meetings seem most effective.
A2.notes.Q7: Personalized support should be more selective to ensure quality.
A2.Q8.1: Consider the impact on student-advisor relationships and long-term trust.

A3.notes.Q3: Course performance and admissions data can be useful, but Absalon data feels intrusive. Sensitive data should only be used if necessary.

A3.notes.Q5: Ensuring the model works equally well across groups is important to avoid perpetuating inequalities.
A3.notes.Q6: Personalized outreach and continuous monitoring are essential for timely support.
A3.notes.Q7: Balanced approach is best for general information, but personalized messages should be more selective to ensure meaningful support.
A3.Q8.1: The impact on student advisor workload and the potential for over-reliance on automated systems are important considerations.
